question: The Society of Righteous and Harmonious Fists was a Chinese secret society that played a key role in ***which 1899–1901 rebellion against foreign powers***?
The black and goopy herbal liqueur Unicum and a red wine known as ‘Bull’s Blood’ are drinks that originate in ***which country***?
While not the capital, Douala is the biggest city and the economic hub of ***what African nation***?
The Eagles, a team from ***which US city***, won this year’s Super Bowl?

One of the three top-selling singles of the 1960s that wasn’t a Beatles song, ‘Release Me’, was a 1967 number one hit for ***which singer***, who began his career under the name Gerry Dorsey and represented the UK at Eurovision in 2012?
Archibald Leach was the given name of ***which English-born Hollywood star*** of the 1930s, ’40s and ’50s?
Famous for its royal castle, ***what is the only English town*** whose name appears in the title of a play by William Shakespeare?

The Universities of Manchester, Leeds and Reading are among those known by a term named after ***what building material***? The term arose contrasting this building material to the stone masonry of older universities.

Alex Ferguson managed ***which Scottish Premier League team*** to the league title in 1984–85, the most recent time a team not from Glasgow has won the league? This club plays home games at Pittodrie.
A leading cause of death, blindness, urinary tract infection and infertility in koalas, ***which bacterial genus*** also causes sexually transmitted diseases and trachoma in humans?
Symbolised by a cup of steaming coffee and sharing its name with an Indonesian Island, ***which computer programming language*** with a four-letter name was created in 1995 by James Gosling?

The Band, later renamed Greatest Days, and Never Forget are two musicals that use the music of ***which boy band*** formed in 1990? The musical The Band was originally cast by the BBC talent show Let It Shine.
The Kenya Land and Freedom Army, who rebelled against the British in Kenya in the 1950s, was more commonly known by ***what name***?
Cotonou is the biggest city and the seat of government, although not the capital, of ***what West African nation***?
***Which city in eastern Poland*** gave its name to the political union of 1569 that established the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth?
The sculptor Mitzi Cunliffe designed the mask-shaped trophies awarded at ***which entertainment award shows***?

***Which teenage actor*** plays the role of Ollie, the son of Daisy May Cooper’s character, in the BBC sitcom Am I Being Unreasonable? He won a BAFTA for Best Male Comedy Performance for the role in the show’s first series in 2023.
***What word*** precedes ‘distillation’ in a process, typically using a multi-layered column, that separates a mixture of liquids based on their different boiling points?
***Who was the third and youngest wife*** of the prophet Muhammad? He died in her arms in 632 CE, and her father Abu Bakr became the first caliph to succeed Muhammad.
***Which is the southernmost of all Chinese provinces***? An island province that was formerly part of Guangdong, it was designated a free-trade zone in 2020.
Established as the first HIV and AIDS charity in the UK, ***which trust*** is named for the first person in Britain known to have died from AIDS-related illnesses in 1982?
***Which darts player***, the current world number 1 and former world champion, currently sits second behind Luke Littler in the Premier League Darts standings?
The 1914 short story collection Dubliners was a work by which great Irish novelist?
Specialising in peri-peri chicken, the restaurant chain Nando’s was founded in ***which country***?
Bought by Kenneth C. Griffin for $200 million, the fifth most expensive painting ever sold is Number 17A, a drip painting by ***which abstract expressionist***?

***Which Dutch physicist*** gives his name to the force law that describes the interaction of a charged particle with both electric and magnetic fields? He is also known for his namesake transformations in special relativity.
Prince William is the current heir to the British throne; assuming he keeps the name William, ***what regnal number*** will he have upon being crowned?
I’m Still Here, which won Best International Feature Film at the recent Academy Awards (2025 y), was directed by a film maker from ***which country***?
The Battle of Sluys [sloyz], fought in June 1340 between a French fleet led by Hugues Quiéret and an English fleet led by King Edward III, was one of the first engagements in ***what conflict***?
The wedding dress that the future Queen Elizabeth II wore to marry Prince Philip was designed by  ***which fashion designer***, who served as her main dressmaker throughout the 1950s?
Greylag, Canada and Egyptian are all species of ***what waterbirds***?
First imposed during the mid-1300s, ***what was the name of the extremely unpopular tax levied on salt*** by the French monarchy? Surprisingly, it was not repealed until 1946.
Heilongjiang [hay-long-jyang] is the northernmost and easternmost of all Chinese provinces; ***what city***, known for its ice sculpture festival, is the capital of Heilongjiang?
***Who*** played the lead role of DCI Jane Tennyson in the UK TV drama series Prime Suspect, originally broadcast between 1991 and 2006?
Known for her great devotion to the prophet, ***who was the first wife of Muhammad*** in Islamic tradition? Like her daughter Fatima, she is considered one of the four ‘Ladies of Heaven’.

***What pair of words*** did Carl Jung use to refer to the unconscious feminine side of a man and the unconscious masculine side of a woman? One of these terms is also used for a feeling of enmity or ill will.
The word ‘piste’ is also used to describe the 14-metre long playing area in ***which two-person combat sport***? In this sport, the piste is marked with two en garde lines.

What name is given to the carved pumpkins, typically housing a light source, that are commonly part of Halloween decorations? They derive from the earlier tradition of carving root vegetables into figures known as punkies in some areas.
In metallurgy, ***what process*** involves reheating a hardened metal to a specific temperature and then cooling it to improve its toughness, and to reduce brittleness?
The Reverend Samuel Parris, the minister of Salem, appears in ***which 1953 Arthur Miller play***? Written as a response to McCarthyism in the US, it shares its name with a famous sporting venue.
Flow, which won Best Animated Feature Film at the recent Academy Awards, was directed by a film maker from  ***which European country***?
Specialising in fried chicken, the fast food chain Jollibee was founded in ***which country in southeast Asia***?

Believed to have been bought by Kenneth C. Griffin, the seventh most expensive painting ever sold is No. 6 (Violet, Green and Red), a color field painting by ***which Latvian-born abstract expressionist***?
Tom Hanks voices Sheriff Woody in ***which Pixar film*** and its sequels?
explanation: TOY STORY (accept any Toy Story film)

question: In economics, the concept describing the relationship between a nation’s investment in defence and its civilian investment is known as ‘Guns versus …’ ***what foodstuff***?
In geology, ***what name*** is given to the process by which one tectonic plate moves under another one and so sinks into the mantle as the plates collide?

Its name being that of the noble title of the eldest illegitimate child of Charles II, ***what is the name of the 1685 rebellion*** against the rule of James II that was put down at the Battle of Sedgemoor?
Which American country singer released the best-known version of the song ‘The Gambler’ in 1978?
***Who*** won the Academy Award for Best Actress in 1975 for her role as Nurse Ratched in the film One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest?

***What English city*** names a type of man’s shoe normally made from black or brown leather, which is characterised by having eyelets underneath the vamp and a closed lacing? They can either be plain or have decorations known as ‘brogueing’.
